note: Frame rects are [x, y, w, h] into the sheet. 'fps' drives the in-browser animation. 'mirror' means left-facing is a horizontal flip in-engine.

groups.name: Actors & Critters
groups.blurb: Everything with a brain. All 13 species live in one registry; each acts only through the same action gateway as the player.

entities.name: Farmer
entities.desc: The player character. Walks the farm and performs every player verb — clearing, tilling, planting, watering, harvesting, collecting, selling, refilling, buying, taking tools, sleeping.
entities.layout: 48px 4x4 grid — row per direction (down, up, left, right), 4-frame walk, column 0 is the standing idle. Column 3 of the up row doubles as the sleeping pose on the cot.

entities.name: Neighbour
entities.desc: The departing child of the cold open: she tills, plants, and waters a demo plot while the player watches, then opens the gate, waves, and leaves the map — the farm is inherited, not given.
entities.layout: Same 4x4 layout as the farmer — the sheet is a palette remap (teal hair, green outfit), not a fresh generation.

facts.Note: Deregistered the moment she opens the gate

entities.name: Chicken
entities.desc: The toy, not a chore. Wanders the yard, lays an egg on a coin flip at the day turn, and clucks when tapped. (Whether the coin flip stays is an open question for the CEO — Q-50.)
entities.layout: 16px single row: cells 0–3 walk right, cells 4–7 the same walk facing left — the one creature that carries its own left frames instead of mirroring.

entities.name: Crow
entities.desc: The joke, not the threat. Flies in on a daily schedule, prefers acorns over crops, eats one thing, and flees any scare. One chance per day — shooing it is a win, not a reprieve.
entities.layout: Perched (while eating), wings up, wings down — a 2-frame flap in flight.

facts.Diet: acorns first, crops when the stock runs dry

entities.name: Sprinkler
entities.desc: The first machine. A static actor that never moves; at the day turn its brain issues ordinary water actions over its radius — automation through the exact same gateway as a thumb.
entities.layout: Two state cells (idle, spraying) — a threshold swap, not an animation; the spray frame holds ~1.4s after the day turn.

facts.Status: built and tested; nothing places one yet (debut awaits a design ruling)

entities.name: Ant Scout
entities.desc: Wanders until it finds a crop, then walks home laying a scent trail for the foragers. Has no verbs at all — it only moves and deposits. Stompable.
entities.layout: A 2-frame walk facing right; left is a mirror.

entities.name: Ant Forager
entities.desc: Follows the scout's scent gradient, takes exactly one crop, and carries it home — reinforcing the trail as it goes. The raid mechanic in miniature.
entities.layout: A 2-frame walk — the scout carrying a pea; left is a mirror.

entities.name: Rabbit
entities.desc: Garden thief. Smells a crop within five tiles, hops over, and takes a bite — but bolts whenever the player comes within three tiles. Not stompable; your footsteps are the counterplay.
entities.layout: A 4-frame hop; left is a mirror.

entities.name: Kangaroo
entities.desc: The rabbit over the fence — same brain, same senses, one difference: its hop crosses fences, hedges, and closed gates. The pest that makes walls insufficient.
entities.layout: A 4-frame hop, same cadence as the rabbit; left is a mirror.

entities.name: Songbird
entities.desc: Pure charm. Drifts across the farm, perches, drifts on. Zero verbs — its brain can never return an action, so it never appears in a replay log. The farm's ambient life.
entities.layout: Perched, wings up, wings down — a 2-frame flap in flight.

entities.name: Mole
entities.desc: Travels under the farm ignoring all terrain, surfaces on a freshly-sown tile, eats the seed, and goes back down. Stompable only in the seconds it is surfaced — its mound stays visible while it travels.
entities.layout: Three state cells (mound, emerging, surfaced), shown here as a cycle.

entities.name: Worm
entities.desc: The slowest thing in the game. Hunts crops and grows a body segment for every crop eaten — its own lengthening body becomes its main obstacle. Stompable on any tile it occupies. Not an animation cycle: the renderer draws one part per occupied tile, mirroring and rotating the directional parts to follow the path and drawing the symmetric cell as a joint at bends.
entities.layout: Head, body, tail, vertical-body/joint parts, assembled one per occupied tile (the only multi-cell actor). Directional parts mirror leftward and rotate 90° for vertical travel; a bend draws the symmetric cell as a knuckle. The preview shows a bent worm exactly as the game renderer assembles it.

facts.Bends: joint cell at corners; head/tail rotate for vertical travel

entities.name: Bot
entities.desc: The scripted automation line and the phase-4 promise. One species, three configs — follow, circle, shoo — carrying the full player verb set (the same array, not a copy). Nothing in the game hands one out yet.
entities.layout: Generated to the farmer's exact 4x4 layout so it reuses the player's draw path verbatim.

facts.Rule: a bot gets no verb the player lacks

groups.name: Crops & Growables
groups.blurb: One shared sheet, one row per crop, four columns of growth. The animation here is the plant growing.

entities.name: Wheat
entities.desc: The first crop and the tutorial's spine. Three days seed to harvest, 5 coins in, 15 out.
entities.layout: The four visual growth stages (seed, sprout, mid-growth, ready).

entities.name: Tomato
entities.desc: The second crop — slower and richer. Unlocks in the shop after the first wheat harvest.
entities.layout: Four growth stages.

entities.name: Pea
entities.desc: Shipped with the actor system as an ordinary crop, but deliberately absent from the crop order — so no shop or HUD path lists it yet. A crop waiting for its debut.
entities.layout: Four growth stages. (Its shop-icon column still points at the coin — the documented trap in the crop defs.)

entities.name: Egg
entities.desc: Inventory item, not a crop — laid by the chicken at the day turn, collected with a tap, sold for 10 coins. Has no growth art because it doesn't grow.
entities.layout: One cell — also the renderer's fallback picture for any small object it has no region for.

entities.name: Scarecrow
entities.desc: A placeable object bought in the shop: protects a radius, and any crow that gets close flees. Collectable back into inventory and placeable again.
entities.layout: Cell 2 of shop_icons.png — its shop icon and its world sprite are deliberately the same picture.

groups.name: Tools
groups.blurb: Six tools, one icon strip. The axe and pickaxe are earned — each sits visible at its parcel gate until its proof fires.

entities.name: Hands
entities.desc: Clears weeds and harvests ripe crops. The tool you always have.
entities.layout: tool_icons.png cell 0.

entities.name: Axe
entities.desc: Clears logs and trees. Earned after 5 harvests — it waits at its parcel gate as a silhouette until then.
entities.layout: tool_icons.png cell 1; the same cell is drawn in-world at its pickup spot.

entities.name: Pickaxe
entities.desc: Clears rocks. Earned after 3 logs cleared; opens the parcel behind it.
entities.layout: tool_icons.png cell 2.

entities.name: Hoe
entities.desc: Tills cleared ground into soil. Refuses politely on the yard — home ground can't be farmed, by design.
entities.layout: tool_icons.png cell 3.

entities.name: Watering Can
entities.desc: Waters seeded and growing tiles. Eight charges, refilled at the well; its icon doubles as the well's purpose pip.
entities.layout: tool_icons.png cell 4.

entities.name: Seed Pouch
entities.desc: Plants into tilled soil. Planting is free — the day's clock only moves for real work.
entities.layout: tool_icons.png cell 5; doubles as the seed box's purpose pip.

groups.name: Stations & Objects
groups.blurb: The fixed furniture of the farm — each one owns a verb, and each has learned to announce what it's for.

entities.name: Cot
entities.desc: Tap to sleep and end the day. The most-worked-on object in the game: it glows at dusk, halos a near-miss tap, tucks her in before the fade, and has a HUD button that taps it for you.
entities.layout: A tall 16x32 cell; the second cell (blanket turned down) swaps in at dusk under one of the Look Lab treatments.

entities.name: Well
entities.desc: Refills the watering can, free. Shows a watering-can pip after your first sip of water is spent.
entities.layout: Tall 16x32 cell.

entities.name: Seed Box (Shop)
entities.desc: Opens the shop — the one screen that had to work with zero words: crop icons and coin counts only. Never shows its pip when you can't afford the cheapest seed.
entities.layout: Tall 16x32 cell.

entities.name: Shipping Bin
entities.desc: Sells the basket at a tap — the whole economy's exit. Wears a coin pip from your very first crop.
entities.layout: Standard 16px cell.

entities.name: Acorn
entities.desc: A finite stock of eight near the trees, never regenerating. Crows prefer them to crops — a mercy with a countdown — and the player can pick them up to hurry the countdown along.
entities.layout: Standard 16px cell.

groups.name: Terrain & Obstacles
groups.blurb: The ground itself and the things standing in the way of a farm.

entities.name: Obstacle Set
entities.desc: Rock (pickaxe), log (axe), weed (hands), tree (axe) — plus the boundary grammar: fence, hedge, closed gate, open gate. 'Not yet' is always a hedge you can see, never a refusal you can't read.
entities.layout: Eight cells in one row: rock, log, weed, tree, fence, hedge, gate closed, gate open.

entities.name: Field Grassland
entities.desc: The open field — the ground a hoe can open. Tall standing blades (generated, Q-70 ruling 2026-09-02): wild grassland against the yard's tidy lawn, so the fence line differs in pattern as well as color.
entities.layout: A 3x3 arrangement of one seamless 16px tile.

facts.Replaced: terrain_grass.png as the field's ground (Q-70); the old tile remains as the yard's derivation source

entities.name: Yard Ground
entities.desc: Home ground: walkable like the field, but no hoe ever opens it. Derived from the original grass tile — tended-lawn colors on a quiet noise pattern. Since Q-70 the field beyond the fence is tall generated grassland, so the boundary is unmistakable.
entities.layout: The grass tile recolored by a script — derived, never independently generated.

facts.Consequence: the first till of every game is beyond the gate

entities.name: Home Floor
entities.desc: The player's home floor: wood planks derived from the fence's own browns, so indoor wood and outdoor wood are the same wood. Walkable, never tillable — the yard's rule, indoors.
entities.layout: A 3x3 arrangement of one seamless 16px plank tile — the terrain_grass.png format.

entities.name: Walls & Window
entities.desc: The home's shell: plaster wall with a wood baseboard, and the window — the same wall with sky through glass. Both are boundary tiles like the fence and hedge: never walkable, drawn edge to edge.
entities.layout: interior.png — cell 0 wall, cell 1 window. The pane's blue is the one new colour: no ambient tile in the game is blue, so it reads as outdoors seen from indoors.

facts.Walkable: never — boundary states, like the fence
facts.Windows: wall variant; more furnishings come later

entities.name: Tilled Soil (Autotile)
entities.desc: Tilled and watered soil as a full autotile set — one 16px tile per neighbor mask, with a parallel watered block. The lookup is the identity function on the mask.
entities.layout: 512x256: dry block in columns 0–15, watered block offset 16 columns right. Alternating here between dry and watered corners.

groups.name: Drawn but Unshipped
groups.blurb: Art that exists with no species row, no brain, no renderer — candidates waiting for a design ruling.

entities.name: Fox, Duck & Squirrel
entities.desc: Three finished sprites sitting in the critter sheet's spare row. No species row references them; they cost nothing to keep and are ready the day a phase-2 ruling gives one of them a job.
entities.layout: The art bench's spare row, now its own sheet.

facts.Status: no brain, no registry row — pure potential
